title: Recipe 69 — Deploying the real loop (dev → edge → a host that stays up)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “Three deployment targets, and the honest limits of each — including one the compiler refuses to emit.”
beats.script: We’re opening the full walkthrough before changing anything, keeping the explanation and the implementation side by side. [[pause:1s]] Three deployment targets, and the honest limits of each — including one the compiler refuses to emit.

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — nothing committed is touched by a take.
beats.script: We’re preparing a clean scratch state for “Start from a blank spec,” so this section starts from a repeatable baseline. [[pause:800ms]] live/ is scratch — nothing committed is touched by a take. The committed starter and walkthrough stay unchanged, which makes another take reproducible.

beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — a real deploy needs a host token on top of the model credential.
beats.script: We’re loading the demo environment into this terminal session; credentials remain in the shell and are never written into the spec. [[pause:1.2s]] Sources demos/.env — a real deploy needs a host token on top of the model credential.

beats.label: Type a harness
beats.cue: “Start from the plainest thing that works. Deployment shouldn't need a special spec.”
beats.script: The driver is copying the exact source-backed lines for “Type a harness” into the scratch artifact now. [[pause:1.2s]] Start from the plainest thing that works. Deployment shouldn't need a special spec.

beats.label: Compile it and check it
beats.cue: “--check before deploy, always. Shipping a bundle you haven't booted is how you find out in production.”
beats.script: The terminal is running “Compile it and check it” now; its output and exit status are the evidence for this beat. [[pause:1s]] --check before deploy, always. Shipping a bundle you haven't booted is how you find out in production.

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok; install ok; boot gated at the provider credentials gate

beats.label: Emit the Cloudflare Worker bundle
beats.cue: “--emit-as cf-worker is a different emitter, not a wrapper. Same spec, a bundle shaped for the edge runtime.”
beats.script: The terminal is running “Emit the Cloudflare Worker bundle” now; its output and exit status are the evidence for this beat. [[pause:1s]] --emit-as cf-worker is a different emitter, not a wrapper. Same spec, a bundle shaped for the edge runtime.
beats.command: crewhaus compile live/crewhaus.yaml -o live/edge --emit-as cf-worker > live/edge.txt 2>&1

beats.label: List what it emitted
beats.cue: “A worker entry point and its manifest. This is what you'd `npm install` and publish.”
beats.script: The terminal is running “List what it emitted” now; its output and exit status are the evidence for this beat. [[pause:1s]] A worker entry point and its manifest. This is what you'd `npm install` and publish.

beats.label: Read the file list
beats.cue: “No Dockerfile, no process manager. The edge target's whole point is that there's nothing to keep alive.”
beats.script: The editor is opening the edge files artifact for “Read the file list,” so we can inspect the concrete artifact on screen. [[pause:1s]] No Dockerfile, no process manager. The edge target's whole point is that there's nothing to keep alive.

beats.label: Diff it against the default bundle
beats.cue: “Everything the emitter changed — read this before assuming your spec ports to the edge unchanged.”
beats.script: The terminal is running “Diff it against the default bundle” now; its output and exit status are the evidence for this beat. [[pause:1s]] Everything the emitter changed — read this before assuming your spec ports to the edge unchanged.
beats.command: diff -r live/dist live/edge > live/emitters.diff; test -s live/emitters.diff

verify.note: the two emitters really do produce different bundles

beats.label: Read the delta
beats.cue: “The recipe is explicit about what doesn't survive the trip: cf-worker cannot run host tools.”
beats.script: The editor is opening the generated diff for “Read the delta,” so we can inspect the concrete artifact on screen. [[pause:1s]] The recipe is explicit about what doesn't survive the trip: cf-worker cannot run host tools.

groups.title: Beat 3 · the limits, stated out loud

beats.label: Read the compile targets
beats.cue: “cli, workflow, graph can emit as cf-worker. The shapes that need a host process can't — and the CLI says so.”
beats.script: The terminal is running “Read the compile targets” now; its output and exit status are the evidence for this beat. [[pause:1s]] cli, workflow, graph can emit as cf-worker. The shapes that need a host process can't — and the CLI says so.

beats.label: Read it
beats.cue: “A deployment target that quietly dropped your tools would be far worse than one that refuses.”
beats.script: The editor is opening the compile help artifact for “Read it,” so we can inspect the concrete artifact on screen. [[pause:1s]] A deployment target that quietly dropped your tools would be far worse than one that refuses.

beats.script: The terminal is running “Read the fly deploy contract” now; its output and exit status are the evidence for this beat. [[pause:1s]] And for the shapes that do need to stay up: a real host, with a real token.
